title: How Can I Sink with Such a Prop
description: How Can I Sink with Such a Prop in Tonic Solfa to ST ANNE, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book II, composed on divine subjects, hymn 116, headed “Mercies and thanks”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST ANNE; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: How can I sink with such a prop As my e-ter-nal God, Who bears the earth's huge pil-lars up, And spreads the heavens a-broad?

lines: How can I sink with such a prop
Who bears the earth's huge pillars up,
How can I die while Jesus lives,
Who rose and left the dead?
Pardon and grace my soul receives
All that I am, and all I have
Whate'er my duty bids me give
Yet if I might make some reserve,
I love my God with zeal so great
That I should give him all.

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST ANNE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
